column1: snob§Nobody thinks of himself as a snob about anything.§没人觉得自己在任何事上是**势利**眼。
soar§The hawk soared for twenty minutes without a wingbeat.§那只鹰**翱翔**了二十分钟，一次也没扇翅膀。
socialize§The cost is socialized and the profit is not.§成本被**社会化**了，利润却没有。
solace§There is a cold solace in knowing the mistake was unavoidable.§得知这个错误无法避免，是一种冰冷的**安慰**。
solemn§A solemn face at a funeral tells you nothing about grief.§葬礼上**肃穆**的表情说明不了什么关于悲伤的事。
solemnize§The marriage was solemnized in a room with eight people.§婚礼在一个只有八个人的房间里**庄严举行**。
solicitous§Solicitous questions from a stranger made her uneasy.§陌生人**关切**的询问让她不安。
solicitude§His solicitude was genuine and slightly exhausting.§他的**关怀**是真诚的，也略微让人吃不消。
solidify§Fat solidifies at a temperature you can feel with a finger.§脂肪在一个手指就能感知的温度下**凝固**。
solitary§Solitary work suits some questions and ruins others.§**独自**工作适合某些问题，却会毁掉另一些。
solvent§Turpentine is the solvent that does the least damage.§松节油是损害最小的那种**溶剂**。
somber§The mood turned somber when the figures were read out.§数字一念出来，气氛就变得**阴郁**。
somnolent§A somnolent afternoon in the archive produced two good pages.§档案室里**昏昏欲睡**的一个下午，写出了两页好东西。
sonorous§The bell is more sonorous now than when it was cast.§这口钟如今比刚铸成时更**洪亮**。
soothe§A soothing tone in a refusal makes it no less a refusal.§拒绝时**语气温和**，并不会让它不再是拒绝。
sophistication§Sophistication about method does not require complicated prose.§方法上的**老练**不需要复杂的文字。
sophistry§Sophistry is an argument that works only on the first hearing.§**诡辩**是只在第一次听时管用的论证。
sophomoric§A sophomoric confidence is the price of learning quickly.§**一知半解的**自信是快速学习的代价。
soporific§A soporific voice ruined an otherwise excellent lecture.§**催眠的**嗓音毁了一场本来极好的讲座。
sovereign§Parliament is sovereign, which is why the question is political.§议会拥有**最高主权**，所以这个问题是政治性的。
spar§A broken spar ended the voyage two days out.§出海两天，一根断掉的**桅杆**结束了这次航行。
spareness§Spareness in a museum label is a kindness to the visitor.§博物馆说明牌的**简省**是对观众的体贴。
sparse§The record is sparse before 1830 and dense after.§一八三〇年之前记录**稀疏**，之后就密集了。
spate§The river was in spate and the ford was impassable.§河水**暴涨**，浅滩无法通过。
spawn§Salmon spawn in the gravel of the upper river.§鲑鱼在上游的砾石中**产卵**。
specificity§Specificity is what turns an anecdote into evidence.§正是**具体性**把轶事变成了证据。
specious§A specious clarity is more dangerous than honest difficulty.§**似是而非的**清晰比诚实的艰涩更危险。
spectacle§He made a spectacle of himself and the meeting ended early.§他**出尽了洋相**，会议提早结束。
speculation§Property speculation emptied the street of families.§房地产**投机**让这条街上的家庭都搬走了。
speculative§A speculative purchase in 1971 funded the whole collection.§一九七一年一次**投机**性的购入，资助了整批藏品。
spellbind§A spellbound audience is not necessarily a persuaded one.§被**迷住**的听众未必是被说服的听众。
spontaneity§Spontaneity in a lecture requires knowing the material cold.§讲座中的**自然发挥**，前提是把材料烂熟于心。
spontaneous§Spontaneous combustion in the hay barn was the official finding.§官方结论是干草仓**自燃**。
sporadic§Sporadic cases appeared for years before anyone connected them.§**零星**病例出现多年，才有人把它们联系起来。
sprawl§He sprawled in the chair and read for four hours.§他**瘫在**椅子里读了四小时。
sprightly§A sprightly opening chapter promises more than the book delivers.§**活泼**的开篇章节许诺的比这本书兑现的多。
spurious§A spurious correlation held up for two decades.§一个**虚假**的相关性维持了二十年。
squalid§There is nothing squalid about being poor and tidy.§贫穷而整洁并不**肮脏**。
squander§Do not squander a good question on a small audience.§不要把一个好问题**浪费**在很小的听众身上。
squelch§Boots squelched through mud for the length of the field.§靴子踩过整块田的泥地，一路**咕唧作响**。
stabilization§Price stabilization worked for two years and then failed loudly.§价格**稳定**政策见效两年，随后轰然失败。
stagnation§Stagnation is harder to notice than decline.§**停滞**比衰退更难察觉。
stalemate§A stalemate in chess is a draw, not a loss.§国际象棋中的**逼和**是平局，不是输。
standard§The gold standard was abandoned and the phrase survived.§**金本位**被废除了，这个说法却留了下来。
standardize§Standardizing the boxes halved the storage cost.§**统一箱子的规格**让仓储成本减半。
startle§Do not startle a horse from behind, however friendly it is.§不管马多温顺，都不要从后面**惊吓**它。
stature§A woman of small stature and considerable presence.§一位**身材**矮小却气场十足的女子。
steadfast§Steadfast in bad weather, he was hopeless in calm.§恶劣天气里他**坚定**不移，风平浪静时却毫无办法。
sternly§The notice sternly forbids what everyone does anyway.§这则告示**严厉**禁止的事，人人照做不误。
stickler§A stickler for form is useful right up until she is not.§一个**拘泥形式**的人很有用，直到她不再有用为止。
stifle§Do not stifle a question because the answer is inconvenient.§不要因为答案不便就**压下**一个问题。
stilted§A stilted translation is often too faithful, not too free.§**生硬**的译文往往是太忠实，而不是太自由。
stimulate§Cold air stimulates the circulation and nothing else.§冷空气只**刺激**血液循环，别无其他。
stimulus§Response to the stimulus takes about a fifth of a second.§对**刺激**的反应大约需要五分之一秒。
stolid§A stolid exterior hid a very quick mind.§**迟钝的**外表下藏着极快的头脑。
strategist§Every strategist looks brilliant in a year that goes well.§顺利的年份里，每个**战略家**看起来都很高明。
stratify§Society stratified along lines the census could not see.§社会沿着人口普查看不见的界线**分层**。
streamline§A streamlined hull saves fuel and costs stability.§**流线型**船体省燃料，却牺牲稳定性。
strenuous§A strenuous walk before breakfast set the tone for the day.§早饭前一次**费力**的步行定下了一天的基调。
strident§Strident advertising made a quiet product look desperate.§**刺耳的**广告让一个安静的产品显得走投无路。
stringent§Stringent conditions kept most applicants away.§**严苛**的条件把大多数申请人挡在了门外。
stunt§The stunt was performed once and never repeated.§这个**特技**只表演过一次，再没重复。
sturdy§A sturdy argument survives a hostile summary.§**结实**的论证经得起充满敌意的概括。
subdue§Subdued colours suit a room that already has a view.§本来就有景观的房间，适合**柔和**的色调。
subordinate§A subordinate clause carries most of the meaning here.§这里的大部分意思由**从句**承载。
